guard: the entry's `branchDigest`: the arms a settled race is never walked into
why: The guard has FOUR separable claims and each is mutated on its own, because a single red would
not say which one carried it: that the digest is WRITTEN, that it is COMPARED, that it is over
STRUCTURE rather than source offsets, and that it covers the LOSERS ONLY.
The last two are narrowness. A digest that refused everything would satisfy the first two
mutations perfectly and make every decided race un-migratable and un-forkable; a digest over the
winner too would replace a divergence naming the step it broke with one naming the whole scope,
which is a worse error for the same event.
This suite counts rather than throws, so a mutation may redden more than the cell it names --
the harness requires the NAMED cell to be red, and the marker prints at the end because the
suite reaches it on every run.

mutations.name: the digest is never written
mutations.expectRed: because the recorded scope entry carries a `branchDigest` over the arms the walk skips
mutations.cell: because the recorded scope entry carries a `branchDigest` over the arms the walk skips
mutations.note: An entry with no digest is compared against nothing -- `if (entry.branchDigest !== undefined)` is how a journal written before this rule stays readable -- so this also silently restores the old blind spot. That is why the WRITE is graded separately from the COMPARISON.

mutations.name: the digest is written but never compared
mutations.expectRed: REPAIRED: an edit inside a branch the race decided now refuses the migration
mutations.cell: REPAIRED: an edit inside a branch the race decided now refuses the migration

mutations.name: source offsets are hashed along with the structure
mutations.expectRed: a REINDENTED losing arm is not an edited one: same structure, same digest, walk completes
mutations.cell: a REINDENTED losing arm is not an edited one: same structure, same digest, walk completes
mutations.note: The first narrowness twin. Acorn nodes carry start/end, so hashing them makes ANY edit earlier in the file diverge a race nobody touched -- the false positive that teaches people to route around a check.

mutations.name: the digest covers every arm, not only the unwalked ones
mutations.expectRed: an edit in the WINNING arm diverges at the STEP it broke, not at the scope
mutations.cell: an edit in the WINNING arm diverges at the STEP it broke, not at the scope
mutations.note: The second narrowness twin, and the subtler one: it does not break the guard, it makes the guard EARLIER than the better check that already exists. The walk enters the winner entry by entry, so an edit there diverges at the step it broke; a digest over the winner pre-empts that with the scope key and loses the location. A guard that fires first is not automatically the right guard.

mutations.name: the comparison is restricted to the migration walk
mutations.replace: if (host.options.migration === true && entry.branchDigest !== undefined && branchDigest !== undefined) {
mutations.expectRed: a RESUME of the same edited source diverges as well, rather than replaying past it
mutations.cell: a RESUME of the same edited source diverges as well, rather than replaying past it
mutations.note: The specified placement is the migrate walk only, so this mutation restores the narrower rule and is still a defect: the run record carries no program hash, so nothing upstream refused edited source before a resume got here, and a settled race is delivered from its entry without entering an arm. The wider placement is deliberate and is graded rather than assumed.

unkillable.name: the `race`-only restriction at the call site
unkillable.why: Widening the call site’s `name === "race"` test to every scope kind adds a digest to `parallel`/`fanOut`, whose branches are ALL walked, and to `conclave`, which a migration cannot enter at all. Nothing observable changes for the first two -- an edit inside a walked branch already diverges at its own step, upstream of any scope-level comparison -- so a mutation on it can only report SURVIVED. It is a cost-and-clarity choice, not a behaviour guard, and is recorded here rather than graded to look like coverage.
